findings.title: The Department of Information Technology (DoIT) did not maintain comprehensive records of telecommunications resource sharing agreements. Certain arrangements regarding the related lease payments, such as the depositing of payments into escrow accounts outside of the State’s control, were inconsistent with DoIT’s understanding of the requirements of State law. DoIT did not take timely action to address these arrangements.
findings.description: DoIT did not maintain comprehensive records of telecommunications resource sharing agreements or account for activity and related compensation. Lease payments were deposited into escrow accounts outside State control instead of the MITDP Fund, inconsistent with State law requirements. DoIT became aware in April 2011 but took no timely action until July 2015.

dollar_amounts.context: related compensation valued as of June 2016
deposits into escrow accounts February 2001 through June 30, 2016
withdrawals from escrow accounts February 2001 through June 30, 2016
balances in escrow accounts as of June 30, 2016

findings.recommendation: DoIT should maintain a comprehensive record of all telecommunications resource sharing agreements administered by State agencies under its jurisdiction, maintain copies of those agreements, and require the agencies to periodically report the status of the agreements; discontinue use of the escrow accounts; working with DSP and DNR, determine the disposition of the remaining escrow account funds and all future resource sharing agreement lease payments; evaluate whether there is any recourse or action to be taken if it is determined that escrow funds should have been deposited into the MITDP Fund.

findings.title: DoIT, DSP, and DNR did not maintain comprehensive records of resource sharing agreements for their own telecommunications towers, properly execute or obtain required approvals for renewals, nor maintain records of equipment attached to their towers.
findings.description: The Departments did not maintain a complete list of resource sharing agreements, missed opportunities to negotiate payment terms on agreements in existence for approximately 20 years, and informally exercised renewal options without proper approval. None maintained complete inventory lists detailing the type and ownership of equipment attached to telecommunications towers.

dollar_amounts.context: value of renewal options exceeding BPW approval threshold
potential loss of compensation from agreements allowed to continue without receiving any compensation

findings.recommendation: DoIT, DSP, and DNR should maintain a comprehensive record of their resource sharing agreements and copies of any renewal options exercised; review existing agreements and determine whether the terms should be renegotiated, ensure new agreements as well as renewals valued at $200,000 or more are retroactively submitted to BPW for approval; establish and maintain complete inventory records of all equipment attached to State-owned telecommunications towers under their jurisdiction.

findings.title: The financial transactions pertaining to escrow account funds were not recorded in the State’s accounting records and were not monitored by State officials, and related interest earnings were retained by the law firm. DSP and DNR personnel did not ensure that account disbursements agreed with the amounts of related purchases.
findings.description: Financial transactions for escrow accounts were not recorded in State accounting records or monitored through the budget process. Interest earned on escrow accounts totaling approximately $90,900 was retained by the law firm instead of paid to the State. DSP and DNR personnel did not verify that disbursements agreed with amounts of related purchases.

dollar_amounts.context: deposits of lease payments into escrow accounts February 2001 to June 2016
disbursements for purchase of goods and services from escrow accounts February 2001 to June 2016
accumulated interest earnings on the escrow accounts retained by law firm

findings.recommendation: DoIT, DSP, and DNR should determine the proper method for recording any current fiscal year escrow account revenue and expenditure transactions in the State’s accounting records; obtain all bank statements for escrow accounts until they are closed and verify the propriety of all transactions; determine whether the State can recover any interest retained by the law firm; to the extent practical, obtain and review invoices for purchases made with escrow account funds.

findings.title: DoIT, DSP, and DNR did not ensure that all compensation due under the resource sharing agreements was collected and, consequently, certain payments were not received.
findings.description: The Departments did not have processes to ensure all compensation due from resource sharing agreements was received. Estimated value of uncollected compensation totaled $917,000. For eight agreements, approximately $342,000 of required lease payments was not received. Two agreements had no compensation received for periods dating back to May 2003.

dollar_amounts.context: payments collected outstanding since fiscal year 2002
estimated value of uncollected compensation
compensation not received for eight resource sharing agreements
potential loss of compensation from two agreements allowed to continue without receiving any compensation

findings.recommendation: DoIT, DSP, and DNR should establish procedures to ensure that all lease payments due from resource sharing agreements are received; determine the amount of unpaid compensation for all 10 resource sharing agreements and take necessary actions to collect the amounts.

findings.title: Purchases made by DSP and DNR from the escrow accounts were not subject to supervisory approval and were not made in accordance with State procurement regulations, and no other attempts were made to ensure that the best value was received.
findings.description: Purchases of equipment and services using escrow account funds were not subject to independent supervisory review or approval. Purchases were not competitively procured or made in accordance with State procurement regulations. One DSP employee directed purchases totaling $258,800 that could have been purchased for approximately $184,700 through Statewide contracts.

dollar_amounts.context: disbursed from escrow accounts for purchases made by law firm on behalf of DSP and DNR February 2001 to June 2016
purchases reviewed totaling approximately January 2011 through June 30, 2016
cost of specific piece of telecommunications equipment purchased from vendor
total cost if purchased through Statewide contracts
savings not realized due to purchases from escrow funds instead of Statewide contracts

findings.recommendation: DSP and DNR should continue abiding by the current prohibition on the use of the escrow account funds; determine the extent to which retroactive approval should be obtained from the Board of Public Works, the Department of Budget and Management, and DoIT for previous purchases from escrow funds.

findings.title: The DNR employee who directed escrow account purchases authorized the use of escrow funds for certain questionable activity related to the purchase and installation of a telecommunications tower on DNR land.
findings.description: A DNR employee authorized payment to an out-of-State vendor without formal approval or proper procurement. The vendor was disqualified from original solicitation but paid $88,500 for work including $73,350 from escrow funds. Total project cost was approximately $138,400. Employee terminated in April 2016.

dollar_amounts.context: disbursed from escrow account to vendor for tower installation
paid to vendor for tower maintenance services July 2011 to November 2015
total paid to vendor for tower installation work
total cost of the tower installation project
from escrow funds for tower installation
paid via State’s corporate purchasing card for tower installation
payments appearing to be inappropriately paid to vendor

findings.recommendation: DNR should submit the tower installation award to DoIT for retroactive review and approval; in consultation with the Office of the Attorney General, determine the extent to which any of the payments totaling $13,400 were inappropriately paid to the vendor and pursue recovery.

findings.title: The DNR employee who directed escrow account purchases processed a unique arrangement with a telecommunications company without review and approval from either DNR management or DoIT. The related payments were deposited into an escrow account and were used to purchase equipment without a competitive procurement and without DNR and control agency approvals.
findings.description: A DNR employee processed an arrangement where a telecommunications company paid DNR $162,000 to vacate licenses for radio frequencies. Funds were deposited into an escrow account instead of the MITDP Fund as required by law and used to purchase equipment without competitive procurement or approvals.

dollar_amounts.context: payment from telecommunications company to vacate licenses

findings.recommendation: DNR and DoIT should review the aforementioned arrangement to determine whether State contract requirements have been met, the terms promote the best interests of the State, and the agreement is properly approved and executed.

findings.title: DSP and DNR did not record, tag, and inventory equipment purchased with escrow account funds and could not readily determine the location of all equipment purchased.
findings.description: DSP and DNR did not record, tag, or inventory equipment purchased with escrow account funds. DSP reviewed purchases totaling approximately $625,600 but review was incomplete as of June 30, 2016. DNR performed a physical inventory for items installed on select towers.

dollar_amounts.context: equipment purchases reviewed by DSP with escrow funds January 1, 2013 to August 31, 2015
purchases made with escrow funds during period DNR physical inventory compared

findings.recommendation: DSP and DNR should expand the aforementioned inventory reviews to identify all equipment purchased with escrow account funds; tag and record located equipment in the inventory records; take appropriate corrective action for any equipment that cannot be located.

extraction.agency_response_summary: DoIT, DSP, and DNR generally agreed with the findings and recommendations. DoIT concurred on most points but disagreed that it made use of escrow agreements itself. DSP and DNR agreed to all applicable recommendations regarding recordkeeping, procurement, inventory, and recovery actions.
extraction.extraction_notes: Audit period based on transaction scope February 2001 through June 30, 2016. Criminal referral confirmed for Findings 6 and 7. Fraud hotline origin not explicitly stated.
